body:
Purpose and Union ministry

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) was approved in February 2019 to promote solar energy in the agricultural sector. Its nodal Union ministry is the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), while designated State agencies and distribution utilities implement the relevant components.

The programme addresses several related agricultural electricity requirements: operating irrigation pumps without conventional grid connections, adding solar generation to existing grid-connected agricultural arrangements, and enabling farmers or their organisations to produce electricity for sale.

PM-KUSUM is not a single uniform subsidy for all agricultural solar equipment. Its Components A, B and C have different beneficiaries and mechanisms.

Component A: Decentralised grid-connected power plants

Component A supports decentralised renewable electricity-generation plants generally having a capacity of 500 kW to 2 MW. Eligible participants can include individual farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives, panchayats, Farmer Producer Organisations and Water User Associations.

The electricity generated by these plants is supplied to the grid and purchased by the relevant DISCOM at the applicable tariff approved by the State Electricity Regulatory Commission. Where a farmer cannot independently develop a plant, arrangements involving a developer and land leasing may be possible under the scheme.

The distinguishing feature is the production of electricity for the distribution grid. Component A is not principally a programme for giving each farmer a small standalone irrigation pump.

Component B: Standalone solar agricultural pumps

Component B supports eligible farmers in installing standalone solar agricultural pumps, particularly in off-grid areas where grid electricity is not available. The normal supported pump-capacity limit is up to 7.5 horsepower (HP).

Instead of depending on a conventional electricity feeder for pumping, a standalone solar pump uses electricity generated locally by solar panels. This makes Component B particularly relevant to farms without feasible grid supply.

Under the standard financial-assistance arrangement for general-category States such as Gujarat, the Union subsidy is 30% of the applicable benchmark or tender cost, whichever is lower; the State subsidy is ordinarily at least 30%; and the farmer meets the remaining amount, normally up to 40%. Bank financing may reduce the amount the farmer must pay initially.

These percentages describe the standard arrangement, not an unconditional promise that every State and every project receives identical support. MNRE also permits implementation without State subsidy, with 30% Union assistance and 70% farmer contribution in general-category States, and special-category regions have different central-assistance rates.

Component C: Solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps

Component C concerns agricultural connections that are already associated with the electricity grid. It has 2 important forms:

  • Individual Pump Solarisation (IPS): Solar panels are associated with an existing grid-connected agricultural pump. The farmer can use solar electricity for irrigation and, under the approved arrangement, sell surplus electricity to the DISCOM.
  • Feeder-Level Solarisation (FLS): A solar-generation system supplies the requirements of an agricultural feeder. Farmers connected to that feeder may receive daytime electricity without each farmer necessarily installing an individual solar system.

Comparing the components

ComponentTypical beneficiaryMain benefitGrid relationship
AFarmers or eligible rural organisationsDevelop 500 kW–2 MW renewable plants and sell powerGrid-connected generation
BEligible farmers without grid supplyStandalone solar irrigation pumpOff-grid pumping
C: IPSFarmers with grid-connected pumpsSolarise an individual agricultural pumpExisting grid connection retained
C: FLSAgricultural feeder consumersSolar-based feeder supplySolarisation at feeder level

Gujarat's role

Gujarat participates in PM-KUSUM as a State implementing the Union programme. The Gujarat Government's Development Programme 2024–25 specifically described support for Component B standalone solar agricultural pumps for off-grid irrigation. This makes PM-KUSUM a relevant example of a Central Sector scheme implemented through State institutions.

Understanding the programme's status in 2026

MNRE's published general scheme period was stated as ending on 31 March 2026. However, that date does not mean all sanctioned PM-KUSUM implementation work stopped immediately.

An MNRE Office Memorandum dated 28 September 2026 extended the deadline for financial closure of eligible Component A and Component C projects to 30 November 2026. It also permitted completion by 31 March 2027 for projects meeting the specified condition that a power purchase agreement had been signed or a notice to proceed had been issued on or before 31 December 2025.

At the 16 November 2026 cutoff, PM-KUSUM must be described with its published scheme period and subsequent implementation extensions. Continuing work on sanctioned projects does not by itself establish that a fresh application window is open for every component or every State.

Prelims focus

  • PM-KUSUM: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan; approved in February 2019.
  • Nodal Union ministry: MNRE.
  • Component A: decentralised grid-connected plants, normally 500 kW–2 MW.
  • Component B: standalone solar agricultural pumps, normally up to 7.5 HP.
  • Component C: solarisation of grid-connected pumps, individually or at feeder level.
  • Trap: The published scheme period ended on 31 March 2026, but eligible sanctioned projects received specified extensions into 2027.

[Sources: MNRE, 'Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan', official scheme description, sections 'Objective', 'Period' and 'Salient Features'; MNRE, National Portal for PM-KUSUM, component descriptions and achievement dashboard dated 30 September 2026; MNRE, Office Memorandum No. 32/645/2017-SPV Division, 28 September 2026, paragraphs 2–3; Government of Gujarat, Development Programme 2024–25, Energy and Petrochemicals Department, Section 2.97, printed p. 66; consulted 16 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: PM-KUSUM: A sells plant power to the grid; B runs an off-grid pump; C solarises an existing grid-connected pump or supplies an agricultural feeder.
pictures.caption: PM-KUSUM contains distinct routes for electricity generation, standalone pumps and grid-connected agricultural supply.

title: PM-KUSUM: Solar Electricity for Agricultural Pumps and Farmers

body:
A Gujarat Government programme

Kisan Suryoday Yojana, also written as Kisan Suryodaya Yojana, is an initiative of the Government of Gujarat for providing electricity to agricultural consumers during daytime hours. It was formally launched on 24 October 2020.

The scheme was developed through Gujarat's energy-sector institutions, including the State's electricity-distribution system. Its principal beneficiaries are farmers receiving electricity through agricultural feeders.

What benefit does the scheme provide?

Many irrigation pumps receive electricity through dedicated agricultural feeders. The utility determines when these feeders receive supply. If electricity is available mainly at night, farmers may need to operate pumps during inconvenient hours.

Kisan Suryoday seeks to provide agricultural electricity during the day by changing the supply arrangements and developing the supporting electricity infrastructure.

The Gujarat Government's Development Programme 2024–25 describes a plan to provide 8 hours of electricity to agricultural feeders during the daytime window from 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

The period from 5:00 AM to 9:00 PM is a 16-hour scheduling window. It should not be read as a promise that each farmer receives an uninterrupted 16-hour supply. The Gujarat budget document specifies 8 hours of supply within that window.

Where did the programme begin?

The initial districts identified for 2020–21 were Dahod, Patan, Mahisagar, Panchmahal, Chhota Udepur, Kheda, Tapi, Valsad, Anand and Gir Somnath. The programme envisaged phased extension to other districts.

The inclusion of Tapi and Valsad among the initial districts is a specific Gujarat fact. The original launch announcement also referred to the development of supporting transmission infrastructure, showing that the programme involved electricity-system arrangements rather than merely distributing equipment to individual farmers.

Difference from PM-KUSUM

Kisan Suryoday and PM-KUSUM both concern agricultural electricity, but they are not interchangeable.

  • Kisan Suryoday: A Gujarat State programme whose immediate benefit is scheduled daytime electricity supply to agricultural consumers.
  • PM-KUSUM Component B: A Union-supported programme under which eligible farmers can receive assistance for standalone solar agricultural pumps.
  • PM-KUSUM Component C: A Union-supported programme for solarising existing grid-connected pumps or agricultural feeders.

A farmer receiving daytime electricity through Kisan Suryoday does not necessarily own an individual solar photovoltaic system. Solar and other renewable-generation facilities may support agricultural electricity supply, but daytime supply and ownership of a solar pump remain different benefits.

Status at the content cutoff

Kisan Suryoday remained a Gujarat State initiative under implementation at the 16 November 2026 cutoff. A Government of India backgrounder dated 23 October 2026 continued to identify it as Gujarat's daytime agricultural-power initiative. Neither its original 2020 announcement nor the dates of its planned phases should be treated as proof that the programme closed.

Prelims focus

  • Kisan Suryoday was launched on 24 October 2020.
  • Government: Gujarat; beneficiaries: agricultural electricity consumers.
  • Main objective: daytime electricity for irrigation.
  • Documented arrangement: 8 hours of supply within the 5:00 AM–9:00 PM daytime window.
  • Tapi and Valsad were among the 10 initial districts identified for 2020–21.
  • Trap: Kisan Suryoday is not itself a scheme granting every farmer a standalone solar pump.

[Sources: Prime Minister's Office, 'PM to Inaugurate Three Key Projects in Gujarat on 24th October', 22 October 2020, PIB Release 1666803, section 'Kisan Suryodaya Yojana'; Government of Gujarat, Development Programme 2024–25, Energy and Petrochemicals Department, Section 2.94, printed p. 66; PIB backgrounder on solar energy in agriculture, 23 October 2026, Release 2327125, section 'State-specific Initiatives'; consulted 16 November 2026.]

pictures.alt: A farmer in Gujarat operates an electric irrigation pump connected to overhead electricity lines as water flows into a field channel in daylight.
pictures.caption: Scheduled daytime electricity allows farmers to operate irrigation pumps during daylight hours.

pictures.alt: The 5:00 AM–9:00 PM scheduling window lasts 16 hours; an agricultural feeder is allotted 8 hours of supply within it.

title: Gujarat Kisan Suryoday: Daytime Electricity for Irrigation

body:
Purpose, launch and authority

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) is a Union programme for improving access to liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) as a cooking fuel among poor households. It was launched on 1 May 2016 at Ballia in Uttar Pradesh.

Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. Connections are provided through the public-sector oil marketing companies and their LPG distributor networks.

PMUY addresses the initial difficulty faced by poor households in obtaining an LPG connection. Its objective is distinct from a programme concerned with electricity supply or rooftop solar generation.

Who is eligible for a PMUY connection?

Under the current Ujjwala connection framework, the principal applicant must meet the following basic conditions:

  • She must be a woman aged at least 18 years.
  • She must belong to an eligible poor household, supported by the prescribed deprivation declaration and other required documentation.
  • There must be no existing LPG connection from an oil marketing company in the same household.

The connection is therefore provided in the name of an eligible adult woman. It is incorrect to describe the programme as an unconditional LPG-connection benefit for every household or as a scheme restricted only to a particular occupation.

What is included in the benefit?

PMUY provides a deposit-free LPG connection. The connection package covers the specified equipment and charges, including the cylinder security deposit, pressure regulator, hose and installation-related items.

Under the Ujjwala 2.0 arrangements, eligible beneficiaries also receive a free first LPG refill and a stove.

First connection benefit and later refill subsidy are different. The free first refill and stove help a household begin using LPG. They do not mean that every subsequent cylinder is supplied free of cost.

Ujjwala 2.0 and migrant households

Ujjwala 2.0 was launched on 10 August 2021 to extend coverage to additional eligible households. It included a simplified arrangement for migrant families, allowing prescribed self-declarations concerning address and family composition where the relevant conventional documents were not available.

Ujjwala 2.0 is a later phase of PMUY, not an entirely unrelated cooking-fuel scheme.

Targeted support for subsequent LPG refills

In addition to the initial connection benefit, the Government has provided targeted subsidies for eligible PMUY consumers' LPG refills. The amount and permitted number of subsidised refills are policy facts that can change by financial year.

For FY 2025–26, a Union Cabinet decision announced on 8 August 2025 approved a subsidy of ₹300 per 14.2 kg cylinder for up to 9 refills per year.

A later Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas statement dated 7 June 2026 described support of ₹300 per 14.2 kg cylinder on the first 4 refills each year. The later statement is the relevant dated description used for this lesson's 16 November 2026 cutoff. The older 9-refill figure must not be presented without its FY 2025–26 qualification.

These figures concern subsidised refills, not the number of cylinders a household is physically permitted to purchase.

Status in 2026

PMUY continued as an active programme at the content cutoff. The official PMUY portal reported 105,685,306 connections released as of 23 September 2026. This figure is an implementation total for that date, not an eligibility rule or a permanent scheme target.

Prelims focus

  • PMUY launched on 1 May 2016; Ujjwala 2.0 launched on 10 August 2021.
  • Nodal ministry: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.
  • Connection applicant: eligible woman aged 18 or above from a poor household.
  • No existing household LPG connection is a basic eligibility condition.
  • Ujjwala 2.0 provides a deposit-free connection, free first refill and stove.
  • Trap: Refill-subsidy limits are date-specific; the June 2026 statement specified ₹300 for the first 4 refills annually.

[Sources: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, official PMUY portal, 'About PMUY', 'Eligibility Criteria' and 'New Ujjwala 2.0 Connection'; Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, PIB Release 2154117, 8 August 2025, targeted subsidy for FY 2025–26; Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, 'Indian Households Continue to Pay Among the Lowest Cooking Gas Prices in the World', PIB Release 2269944, 7 June 2026; official PMUY portal, connection dashboard dated 23 September 2026; consulted 16 November 2026.]
